name: UNIX
description: The Operating System that started it all.
controversy_description: Obviously None.

name: Linux
description: A free and open-source kernel that became the foundation for countless operating systems and distributions.
controversy_description: Occasional disagreements within the kernel development community, including governance disputes and Torvalds' communication style.

name: Debian
description: One of the oldest and most influential Linux distributions, known for stability, strict free software guidelines, and forming the base for many other distros.
controversy_description: Internal debates over systemd adoption and free software purity have caused community splits.

name: Ubuntu
description: A user-friendly Linux distribution based on Debian, designed to make Linux accessible to the mainstream.
controversy_description: Criticized for decisions like the Unity desktop, Amazon search integration, and Snap package prioritization.

name: Fedora
description: A cutting-edge Linux distribution sponsored by Red Hat, serving as a testing ground for technologies that later appear in Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
controversy_description: Known for adopting new technologies early, sometimes causing stability concerns among users.

name: Arch Linux
description: A lightweight, rolling-release Linux distribution focused on simplicity, user control, and minimalism.
controversy_description: Criticized for being difficult for beginners and for occasional breakage due to its rolling-release nature.

name: Gentoo Linux
description: A highly customizable Linux distribution built around source-based package management and user control.
controversy_description: Criticized for long compile times and being too complex for average users.

name: Slackware
description: One of the oldest surviving Linux distributions, known for its simplicity and UNIX-like design.
controversy_description: Criticized for slow release cycles and lack of modern conveniences found in other distros.

name: openSUSE
description: A polished Linux distribution known for YaST, stability, and strong enterprise backing from SUSE.
controversy_description: Some users dislike the heavy reliance on YaST and the split between Leap and Tumbleweed.

name: Manjaro
description: A user-friendly Arch-based distribution offering easier installation and curated rolling updates.
controversy_description: Criticized for occasional repository delays and past team management controversies.

name: Linux Mint
description: A popular Ubuntu-based distribution focused on ease of use, stability, and a traditional desktop experience.
controversy_description: Faced criticism for security delays and its past reliance on unsafe update policies.

name: Kali Linux
description: A Debian-based distribution designed for penetration testing, security research, and digital forensics.
controversy_description: Often misused by beginners, leading to misconceptions about its purpose and security risks.

name: Linux for PlayStation 2
description: An official Linux port for the PlayStation 2, enabling the console to function as a basic computer.
controversy_description: Limited hardware access and poor performance restricted its usefulness.

name: Linux for Wii
description: A community-driven Linux port for the Nintendo Wii, running via exploits and homebrew loaders.
controversy_description: Performance limitations and lack of official support restricted mainstream adoption.

name: Linux for Dreamcast
description: A Linux port for the Sega Dreamcast, showcasing the console’s potential beyond gaming.
controversy_description: Hampered by extremely limited RAM and storage, making it impractical for real use.

name: iPodLinux
description: A Linux distribution ported to early iPod models, enabling games, apps, and custom firmware features.
controversy_description: Apple firmware updates frequently broke compatibility, and development eventually stalled.

name: Pop!_OS
description: A user-friendly Ubuntu-based Linux distribution optimized for creators, developers, and System76 hardware, featuring tiling window management and strong GPU support.
controversy_description: Some users criticized the shift from GNOME to COSMIC due to fragmentation concerns.

name: Elementary OS
description: A visually polished Ubuntu-based distribution inspired by macOS, focusing on simplicity, design consistency, and a curated app ecosystem.
controversy_description: Faced backlash for its pay-what-you-want download model and slow major releases.

name: Zorin OS
description: An Ubuntu-based distribution designed to provide a familiar experience for users transitioning from Windows.
controversy_description: Some users criticized the paywalled 'Ultimate' edition.

name: AlmaLinux
description: A community-driven, binary-compatible replacement for CentOS after Red Hat shifted CentOS to a rolling-release model.
controversy_description: Faced uncertainty after Red Hat restricted access to RHEL source code.

name: Rocky Linux
description: A RHEL-compatible distribution created by CentOS co-founder Gregory Kurtzer as a successor to classic CentOS.
controversy_description: Similar concerns as AlmaLinux regarding RHEL source code access.

name: Funtoo Linux
description: A Gentoo-based distribution created by Gentoo’s original founder, focusing on performance and improved package management.
controversy_description: Criticized for slower updates and smaller community compared to Gentoo.

name: Ubuntu Touch
description: A mobile Linux operating system originally developed by Canonical, later continued by the UBports community.
controversy_description: Canonical’s sudden abandonment of the project caused backlash from early adopters.

name: postmarketOS
description: A Linux distribution for smartphones aiming for a 10-year lifecycle, based on Alpine Linux.
controversy_description: Limited hardware support and slow progress on daily-driver readiness.

name: Sailfish OS
description: A Linux-based mobile OS featuring gesture navigation and partial Android app compatibility.
controversy_description: Criticized for proprietary components and limited device support.

name: Maemo
description: A Linux-based mobile OS used on Nokia Internet Tablets and early smartphones, known for its openness and multitasking.
controversy_description: Discontinued after Nokia shifted to MeeGo and later Windows Phone.
